newsitem.title: UK: Investors in E.Europe need better protection - UK.
newsitem.headline: Investors in E.Europe need better protection - UK.

text.p: Investors in the former communist countries of central and eastern Europe need better protection from unscrupulous business people, Britain's Overseas Development Minister Lynda Chalker said on Monday.
"Opening up economies creates dangers as well as opportunities," she said at the start of the annual meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).

"Quick profits will not necessarily be conducive to growth. This does not imply a return to government economic controls, but means establishing regulatory frameworks that protect the saver and investor from unscrupulous businesses."
The EBRD was set up in 1991 to assist former Soviet bloc countries in the transition to free market economies.
Western investors have been frightened away from some countries in the region because of a perception that insider trading and even fraud are commonplace.

Chalker said there had been many encouraging trends throughout the region -- the market economy model was widely accepted, the pace of political reform had been phenomenal and democracy was taking root.
But she expressed concern about the disparity between the economic front-runners and the laggards.
"I am concerned too about the remaining underlying threats of regional tension, ethnic discord and the resurgence of nationalism," Chalker added.
